Team —

Quick diagnostics after a fast telemetry pass:
- Dedicated GPU pool (gpu-pool-03-us-west) shows sustained 98% utilization on the family of nodes serving Bluecrest models for the last 50 minutes.
- KV cache miss/eviction rates spiked coincident with the latency bump — suggests working set blowout.
- Control plane reports reservation footprint OK but observed pod-level token queueing and backpressure.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a workload pattern change (larger batch-size or higher sequence lengths) from Bluecrest is causing GPU-side contention and catastrophic KV cache churn — this pushes requests into queueing and induces retries/5xx. The reservation accounting at the control plane is accurate, but the dedicated pool is overcommitted at the node level due to packing heuristics + recent noisy neighbor jobs.

Immediate actions I'm taking:
1) Triggering routing policy to divert ~30% of Bluecrest traffic to the warm standby (eu-west warm-pool) and to a lower-cost quantized variant for non-critical endpoints.
2) Requesting ops to bump the pool packing thresholds and drain any known long-tail jobs.
3) Asking for emergency burst (up to 6 GPU slots) to be authorized while we stabilize.

Attaching a short runbook with the burst sequence and rollback steps: burst_activation_steps.md

I'll standby on the bridge to validate metrics as we flip routing.

-David
Sr. Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
